result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_df_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get selected nodes as a Polars DataFrame. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7671-L7768){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_df_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Similar to get_node_df but only exports currently selected nodes. Useful for analyzing subsets of nodes after filtering with selection methods. The DataFrame always includes 'id', 'label', and 'type' as the first three columns, sorted by 'id' in ascending order. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pl.DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : DataFrame with mandatory columns 'id', 'label', 'type' (first three), followed by other attributes and 'degree'. Empty DataFrame if no nodes are selected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Behaves exactly like `get_node_df()` but drains from the current selection rather than the full graph. That means the same column layout (`id`, `label`, `type` first, other attributes in alphabetical order, `degree` last, rows sorted by `id`) and the same `None`-for-missing semantics. If nothing is selected, an empty DataFrame comes back, so remember to run one of the `select_nodes...` methods first. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Only nodes in the current selection appear in the DataFrame -- here, just the high-degree hub of a combined star and path: ::: {#0a2e7688 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(10) .add_path_graph(5) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3) ) df = graph.get_node_df_ws() df.shape[0] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: This makes it easy to run DataFrame analysis on just a subset of the graph: ::: {#61052fed .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") ) a_id = graph.get_id_from_label("A") b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") c_id = graph.get_id_from_label("C") graph.select_nodes_by_id([a_id, b_id, c_id]) graph.get_node_df_ws()["degree"].mean() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1.3333333333333333 ``` ::: :::
